name: Shackleton–de Gerlache connecting ridge
description: Representative point of a region: where the ridge between Shackleton and de Gerlache craters meets the rim of Shackleton, a spot LROC calls of high scientific interest. Connecting Ridge was one of NASA's 13 Artemis III candidate regions in 2022.

name: Malapert Massif
description: Representative point of a region: the flat area LROC calls the heart of the Malapert Massif Artemis III candidate landing region. The massif is thought to be a remnant of the South Pole-Aitken basin rim.

name: Haworth
description: Representative point of a region: the centre of a NASA Ames terrain model of the area beyond the north rim of Haworth crater. Haworth is one of NASA's nine Artemis III candidate regions announced in 2024.

name: Mons Mouton
description: Representative point of a region: the IAU centre of the mountain Mons Mouton. Mons Mouton is one of NASA's nine Artemis III candidate regions announced in 2024.

name: Nobile Rim 2
description: Representative point of a region: the best-ranked landing point in a 2024 multi-criteria study of the Artemis III candidate regions. Nobile Rim 2 is one of NASA's nine Artemis III candidate regions announced in 2024.

name: de Gerlache Rim 2
description: Representative point of a region: the best-ranked point in this region in a 2024 multi-criteria study of the Artemis III candidate regions. de Gerlache Rim 2 is one of NASA's nine Artemis III candidate regions announced in 2024.

name: Amundsen Rim
description: Representative point of a region: the best-ranked point in this region in a 2024 multi-criteria study of the Artemis III candidate regions. Amundsen Rim was one of NASA's 13 candidate regions in 2022 and is not in the 2024 list of nine.

name: Cabeus, LCROSS Centaur impact point
description: Where NASA's LCROSS mission crashed a spent Centaur rocket stage into a permanently shadowed area of Cabeus crater to look for water and other volatiles.

name: Near south pole reference point
description: A test point chosen by the team very close to the south pole, the same point used for the JPL Horizons check. It is not a landing site.

name: IM-2 Athena, Mons Mouton
description: Where Intuitive Machines' Athena lander, carrying NASA CLPS instruments, came to rest on its side in a 20 m crater near the centre of Mons Mouton.

name: Chandrayaan-3 Vikram lander
description: Landing site of ISRO's Chandrayaan-3, about 600 km from the south pole. It shows the high southern latitudes beyond the polar candidate regions.

name: Apollo 11, Tranquility Base
description: First crewed landing on the Moon, in Mare Tranquillitatis. An equatorial near-side site for contrast with the poles.

name: Apollo 15, Hadley-Apennine
description: Apollo 15 landing site at Hadley Rille, at the foot of the Apennine mountains. A mid-latitude near-side site for contrast with the poles.

name: Apollo 17, Taurus-Littrow
description: Apollo 17 landing site in the Taurus-Littrow valley. A near-side valley site for contrast with the poles.

name: SLIM, near Shioli crater
description: Landing site of JAXA's Smart Lander for Investigating Moon, next to the small fresh crater Shioli. A low-latitude near-side site.

name: Chang'e 4, Von Kármán crater
description: Landing site of China's Chang'e 4 in Von Kármán crater on the lunar far side.

name: Chang'e 6, Apollo basin
description: Landing site of China's Chang'e 6 sample return mission, on a mare plain at the southern edge of the far-side Apollo basin.
